title: Recall email list: the DISTINCT is not redundant
prompt: Product recall mailing, run on demand a few times a month and urgent when it runs. Example: prefix 'BAT-2291'
matches 3 SKUs, about 2.1M order lines on 1.6M orders, about 410k customers and about 402k distinct emails. Runtime
about 70 s: the plan builds 2.1M joined rows and does a Sort (Distinct) on the varchar(254) Email with a large
spill. About 2% of emails are shared by several customer rows. The email platform rejects a file that contains an
address twice. Email comparison is case-insensitive (database collation).
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Customers: 2.0M rows. Tier S = 1.85M, G = ~150k, P = 25 partner accounts (CustomerID 1 to 25). IsActive = 1 for 88%. Email is NULL for ~9% (~180k rows, ~160k of them active). About 2% of non-NULL emails are shared by two or more customer rows (households). ReferredByCustomerID is non-NULL for 18%; 312 rows are self-referrals (ReferredByCustomerID = CustomerID, CustomerID 500001 to 500312). AccountNumber always matches 'AC' + 10 digits (CHECK constraint).

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.
OrderLines: 120M rows, 4 per order on average. About 0.3% of orders have no lines.
Products: 40k rows. SKU prefixes group product families, 1-3 SKUs per prefix.
baseline_sql: JOIN qe.Orders o      ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
JOIN qe.OrderLines ol ON ol.OrderID = o.OrderID
WHERE ol.ProductID IN (SELECT p.ProductID FROM qe.Products p WHERE p.SKU LIKE @SkuPrefix + '%')

correct_families.description: A semi join reduces the work to one row per qualifying customer; DISTINCT then removes the emails that several customers share.
reference_sql: JOIN qe.OrderLines ol ON ol.OrderID = o.OrderID
JOIN qe.Products   p  ON p.ProductID = ol.ProductID

traps.why: EXISTS makes customers unique, not emails. The output column is Email, and about 2% of emails belong to several customers.
traps.told_apart_by: Two customers that share one email address and both bought a recalled product.
example_sql: JOIN qe.OrderLines ol ON ol.OrderID = o.OrderID
JOIN qe.Products   p  ON p.ProductID = ol.ProductID

traps.why: GROUP BY CustomerID, Email still returns a shared email once per customer.
traps.told_apart_by: Two customers that share one email address and both bought a recalled product.
example_sql: JOIN qe.OrderLines ol ON ol.OrderID = o.OrderID
JOIN qe.Products   p  ON p.ProductID = ol.ProductID

traps.why: Without c.Email IS NOT NULL, DISTINCT returns one NULL row.
traps.told_apart_by: A customer with a NULL email who bought a recalled product.
example_sql: JOIN qe.OrderLines ol ON ol.OrderID = o.OrderID
JOIN qe.Products   p  ON p.ProductID = ol.ProductID

traps.why: A binary or case-sensitive collation keeps addresses that differ only in case, which the platform treats as duplicates.
traps.told_apart_by: Two customers with the same address in different letter case.
example_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.Email COLLATE Latin1_General_BIN2 AS Email
JOIN qe.OrderLines ol ON ol.OrderID = o.OrderID
JOIN qe.Products   p  ON p.ProductID = ol.ProductID

min_improvement.basis: Provisional: no reference measurement. The sort handles about 410k emails instead of 2.1M joined rows.

key.reference_notes: The existing indexes are enough: UX_Products_SKU, IX_OrderLines_ProductID, and PK_Orders or IX_Orders_OrderDate.
